A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing a plea alleging lack of transparency in notices issued to voters by election authorities in Delhi during SIR. “ Form 6 is for someone seeking enrolment for the first time. Form 8 is for the correction or shifting of residence. Suppose a person was enrolled in Vasant Kunj and has now shifted to Sarita Vihar. That person can disclose the earlier polling booth, electoral roll particulars and voter number, and provide the new address. Why should that person be required to submit Form 6?” CJI Kant asked the ECI today. items.title: NDA sweeps Karnataka Council polls, wins all four seats in setback to Congress
items.summary: In a setback to the ruling Congress, the BJP-JD(S) alliance won all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats that went to polls on October 23, taking both teachers' and both graduates' constituencies. Congress had earlier held one of the four seats. The biggest upset for Congress came in the Bengaluru Teachers' constituency, where five-time MLC and former Deputy Chairman Puttanna lost to NDA candidate AP Ranganath. In the North-East Teachers' constituency, BJP candidate Shashil G Namoshi secured his fifth victory, defeating Congress nominee Sharanappa Mattur. In the West Graduates' constituency, SV Sankanur won his third consecutive term, defeating Congress' Mohan Limbikai. In the South East Graduates' constituency, BJP's KM Suresha defeated Congress candidate Shashi Hulikuntemutt. The results have rejuvenated the NDA partners, who were jolted earlier this year when 11 of its MLAs cross-voted in the June polls to seven Legislative Council seats. Congress won five of those seven seats, while the BJP won two. In May, Congress also retained the Davangere South and Bagalkot bypolls despite strong internal differences. items.title: Bengaluru court sets aside ₹9 crore arbitral award against Karnataka Education Department
items.summary: A Bengaluru commercial court recently set aside an arbitral award directing the Karnataka Department of State Education Research and Training (DSERT) to pay over ₹9 crore to Puthur Infotech in a dispute concerning maintenance services provided to 4,396 schools across the State. [DESERT v. Puthur Info] Judge Vijaya Kumar Rai held that the arbitrator had committed patent illegality by failing to consider the State government's objection that the company's claims were barred by limitation. " The omission to record a finding on limitation is a fundamental defect which goes to the root of the matter and renders the award patently illegal for non-consideration of the defence raised by the respondent ," the Court observed. The dispute arose from a 2013 tender issued by DSERT for maintenance of UPS systems, printers and LCD projectors in 1,763 government high schools and 2,633 aided high schools across Karnataka. Puthur Infotech secured the ₹7.19 crore contract for the period between April 2014 and April 2015.
